bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起昭陽大淵獻，盡重光協洽，凡九年。

translations.literal: From Zhao Yang Da Yuan Xian through Zhong Guang Xie Xie; nine years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhao Yang Da Yuan Xian through Zhong Guang Xie Xie—nine years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，三月，甲午，丞相李蔡坐盜孝景園，堧地，葬其中，當下吏，自殺。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the third month, on jiawu, Chancellor Li Cai was convicted of robbing Emperor Jing's park—embankment land—and burying within it; he was to be handed to the officials and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the third month, on jiawu, Chancellor Li Cai was convicted of seizing embankment land from Emperor Jing's park and burying someone there; he was to be handed over to the officials and took his own life.

sentences.zh: ----2罷三銖錢，更鑄五銖錢。

translations.literal: ----2 The three-zhu coin was abolished and the five-zhu coin was recast.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The three-zhu coin was abolished and the five-zhu coin was recast.

sentences.zh: 於是民多盜鑄錢，楚地尤甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people widely counterfeited coin, and the Chu region was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people widely counterfeited coin, and the Chu region was worst of all.

sentences.zh: 上以為淮陽，楚地之郊，乃召拜汲黯為淮陽太守。

translations.literal: The emperor thought that Huaiyang was on the border of the Chu region and thereupon summoned and appointed Ji An as Governor of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Huaiyang lay on the edge of Chu country and summoned Ji An to be Governor of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 黯伏謝不受印，詔數強予，然後奉詔。

translations.literal: Ji An prostrated himself, declined, and would not accept the seal; the edict repeatedly forced it upon him, and only then did he obey.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An prostrated himself and refused the seal; the edict repeatedly pressed it on him, and only then did he obey.

sentences.zh: 黯為上泣曰：「臣自以為填溝壑，不復見陛下，不意陛下復收用之。

translations.literal: Ji An wept to the emperor, saying: "Your servant thought he would fill ditches and gullies and never again see Your Majesty; he did not expect Your Majesty to take him back into service.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An wept before the emperor, saying, "I thought I would fill some ditch and never see Your Majesty again; I did not expect You to take me back into service.

sentences.zh: 臣常有狗馬病，力不能任郡事。

translations.literal: Your servant often suffers dog-and-horse illness and lacks the strength to bear commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I am often ill and lack the strength to govern a commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣願為中郎。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to serve as a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: I wish only to serve as a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出入禁闥，補過拾遺，臣之願也。

translations.literal: To enter and leave the forbidden gates, mend faults and gather what was omitted—this is your servant's wish.
translations.idiomatic: To pass in and out of the palace gates, mend faults and gather what was omitted—that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「君薄淮陽邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Do you slight Huaiyang?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Do you look down on Huaiyang?

sentences.zh: 吾今召君矣，顧淮陽吏民不相得，吾徒得君之重，臥而治之。

translations.literal: I now summon you only because the officials and people of Huaiyang do not get along; I merely need your weight—I can govern lying down.
translations.idiomatic: I summon you now only because the officials and people of Huaiyang are at odds; I need only your weight—I can govern from my couch.

sentences.zh: 黯既辭行，過大行李息，曰：「黯棄逐居郡，不得與朝廷議矣。

translations.literal: When Ji An had taken leave and was on his way, he called on Grand Herald Li Xi and said: "Ji An, cast out and dwelling in a commandery, can no longer join in court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji An had taken leave and was on his way, he called on Grand Herald Li Xi and said, "Cast out to a commandery, I can no longer join in court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫湯，智足以拒諫，詐足以飾非，務巧佞之語，辯數之辭，非肯正為天下言，專阿主意。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Tang has wisdom enough to reject remonstrance and deceit enough to cover wrongdoing; he devotes himself to crafty flattery and disputatious rhetoric, unwilling to speak uprightly for all under Heaven but devoted solely to pleasing the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Tang has wit enough to reject remonstrance and deceit enough to cover wrongdoing; he traffics in crafty flattery and disputatious rhetoric, unwilling to speak uprightly for the realm but devoted solely to pleasing the ruler's intent.

sentences.zh: 主意所不欲，因而毀之；

translations.literal: What the ruler's intent does not want, he thereupon destroys;
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler does not want, he destroys;

sentences.zh: 主意所欲，因而譽之。

translations.literal: what the ruler's intent desires, he thereupon praises.
translations.idiomatic: what the ruler desires, he praises.

sentences.zh: 好興事，舞文法，內懷詐以御主心，外挾賊吏以為威重。

translations.literal: He loves to raise affairs and twist the written law; inwardly he harbors deceit to master the ruler's heart, outwardly he relies on wicked clerks for awe and weight.
translations.idiomatic: He loves to stir up affairs and twist the written law; inwardly he harbors deceit to master the ruler's heart, outwardly he leans on wicked clerks for power and weight.

sentences.zh: 公列九卿，不早言之，公與之俱受其戮矣。

translations.literal: You stand among the Nine Ministers—if you do not speak of this early, you will together with him suffer execution.
translations.idiomatic: You stand among the Nine Ministers—if you do not speak of this soon, you will perish together with him.

sentences.zh: 」息畏湯，終不敢言；

translations.literal: " Xi feared Tang and in the end dared not speak;
translations.idiomatic: " Xi feared Tang and in the end dared not speak;

sentences.zh: 及湯敗，上抵息罪。

translations.literal: when Tang fell, the emperor held Xi accountable for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: when Tang fell, the emperor held Xi accountable.

sentences.zh: 使黯以諸侯相秩居淮陽，十歲而卒。

translations.literal: Ji An was made to dwell in Huaiyang at the rank of a feudal chancellor and died after ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An held Huaiyang at the rank of a feudal chancellor and died after ten years.

sentences.zh: ----3詔徙奸猾吏民於邊。

translations.literal: ----3 An edict ordered that crafty and violent officials and people be moved to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 An edict ordered crafty and violent officials and people moved to the frontier.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，乙卯，以太子少傅武強侯莊青翟為丞相。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, the Marquis of Wuqiang Zhuang Qingdi, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Marquis of Wuqiang Zhuang Qingdi, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----5天子病鼎湖甚。

translations.literal: ----5 The Son of Heaven was gravely ill at Lake Ding.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 The emperor was gravely ill at Lake Ding.

sentences.zh: 巫醫無所不致，不愈。

translations.literal: Shamans and physicians were sought everywhere, yet he did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans and physicians were sought everywhere, yet he did not recover.

sentences.zh: 游水發根言上郡有巫，病而鬼神下之。

translations.literal: You Shui Fagen said that in Shang Commandery there was a shaman who, when ill, had spirits and gods descend upon him.
translations.idiomatic: You Shui Fagen said that in Shang Commandery there was a shaman who, when ill, had spirits descend upon him.

sentences.zh: 上召置，祠之甘泉，及病，使人問神君，神君言曰：「天子無憂病；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and installed him, sacrificing to him at Ganquan; when he fell ill he sent men to question the Spirit Lord, and the Spirit Lord said: "The Son of Heaven need not worry over illness;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned and installed him, sacrificing to him at Ganquan; when he fell ill he sent men to question the Spirit Lord, who said, "The Son of Heaven need not worry over illness;

sentences.zh: 病少愈，強與我會甘泉。

translations.literal: when the illness eases somewhat, come vigorously to meet me at Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: when it eases somewhat, come in strength to meet me at Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 」於是病癒，遂起幸甘泉，病良已，置酒壽宮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the illness was cured; he thereupon rose and visited Ganquan; the illness was fully gone, and he set out wine at Shou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the illness cleared; he rose and visited Ganquan; when he was fully recovered, he set out wine at Shou Palace.

sentences.zh: 神君非可得見，聞其言，言與人音等，時去時來，來則風肅然，居室帷中。

translations.literal: The Spirit Lord could not be seen; one heard his words, and his speech was the same as a human voice; he came and went at times—when he came the wind was solemn, within the curtains of the dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Spirit Lord could not be seen; one heard his words, and his voice was like any man's; he came and went—when he came the wind turned solemn, within the curtains of the dwelling.

sentences.zh: 神君所言，上使人受，書其言，命之曰「畫法」。

translations.literal: What the Spirit Lord spoke, the emperor had men receive, wrote down his words, and named them "Graphic Method."
translations.idiomatic: What the Spirit Lord spoke, the emperor had men receive and write down, naming the record "Graphic Method."

sentences.zh: 其所語，世俗之所知也，無絕殊者，而天子心獨喜；

translations.literal: What he spoke was what the world ordinarily knows—nothing utterly extraordinary—yet the Son of Heaven's heart alone rejoiced;
translations.idiomatic: What he spoke was what the world ordinarily knows—nothing utterly extraordinary—yet the emperor's heart alone rejoiced;

sentences.zh: 其事秘，世莫知也。

translations.literal: the affair was secret, and the age did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: the affair was secret, and the age knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 時上卒起，幸甘泉，過右內史界中，道多不治，上怒曰：「義縱以我為不復行此道乎！

translations.literal: At that time the emperor suddenly set out and visited Ganquan; passing through the Right Metropolitan Steward's jurisdiction, the roads were largely unmaintained; the emperor angrily said: "Does Yi Zong think I will never again travel this road!
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor suddenly set out for Ganquan; passing through the Right Metropolitan Steward's jurisdiction, he found the roads largely unmaintained and said in anger, "Does Yi Zong think I will never travel this road again!

sentences.zh: 」銜之。

translations.literal: " He harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " He harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，雨水，無冰。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, there was rain water and no ice.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, there was rain instead of snow and no ice.

sentences.zh: ----2上既下緡錢令而尊卜式，百姓終莫分財佐縣官，於是楊可告緡錢縱矣。

translations.literal: ----2 After the emperor had issued the privatized-wealth edict and honored Bu Shi, the common people in the end never divided their property to assist the district officials; thereupon Yang Ke reported privatized wealth on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 After the emperor issued the privatized-wealth edict and honored Bu Shi, the people still would not divide their property to assist the district officials; thereupon Yang Ke reported privatized wealth on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 義縱以為此亂民，部吏捕其為可使者。

translations.literal: Yi Zong thought this disturbed the people and ordered his subordinate officers to arrest those who could be made to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zong thought this disturbed the people and ordered his officers to arrest those who could be pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 天子以縱為廢格沮事，棄縱市。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven regarded Zong as having nullified and obstructed the undertaking and abandoned him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Zong as having nullified and obstructed the undertaking and had him executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: ----3郎中令李敢，怨大將軍之恨其父，乃擊傷大將軍，大將軍匿諱之。

translations.literal: ----3 Director of the Palace Gentlemen Li Gan resented the Grand General for his father's grievance and struck and wounded the Grand General; the Grand General concealed and hushed it.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Director of the Palace Gentlemen Li Gan resented the Grand General for his father's death and struck and wounded him; the Grand General concealed it.

sentences.zh: 居無何，敢從上雍，至甘泉宮獵，驃騎將軍去病射殺敢。

translations.literal: Before long Gan followed the emperor to Yong, hunted at Ganquan Palace, and the Rapid Cavalry General Huo Qubing shot and killed Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gan followed the emperor to Yong and hunted at Ganquan Palace; Rapid Cavalry General Huo Qubing shot and killed him.

sentences.zh: 去病時方貴幸，上為諱，雲鹿觸殺之。

translations.literal: Qubing was then at the height of favor; the emperor made excuse for him, saying a stag had struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing was then at the height of favor; the emperor made excuse for him, saying a stag had struck and killed Gan.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，乙巳，廟立皇子閎為齊王，旦為燕王，胥為廣陵王，初作誥策。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, at the ancestral temple the emperor invested the princes: Hong as King of Qi, Dan as King of Yan, Xu as King of Guangling—the first composition of investiture documents.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, at the ancestral temple the emperor invested Hong as King of Qi, Dan as King of Yan, and Xu as King of Guangling—the first composition of investiture documents.

sentences.zh: ----5自造白金、五銖錢後，吏民之坐盜鑄金錢死者數十萬人，其不發覺者不可勝計，天下大抵無慮皆鑄金錢矣。

translations.literal: ----5 From the time white metal and five-zhu coin were created, officials and people convicted of counterfeiting gold coin who died numbered several hundred thousand; those undetected could not be fully counted—under Heaven, broadly speaking, nearly all cast gold coin.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 From the time of white metal and five-zhu coin, several hundred thousand officials and people died for counterfeiting gold coin; the undetected could not be counted—under Heaven, it seemed nearly everyone cast gold coin.

sentences.zh: 犯者眾，吏不能盡誅。

translations.literal: Offenders were numerous; the officials could not execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders were so numerous the officials could not execute them all.

sentences.zh: ----6六月，詔遣博士褚大、徐偃等六人分循郡國，舉兼併之徒及守、相、為吏有罪者。

translations.literal: ----6 In the sixth month, an edict sent Erudites Chu Da, Xu Yan, and six others in all to tour the commanderies and kingdoms separately, reporting those who merged and swallowed others' holdings, as well as governors, chancellors, and officials guilty in office.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the sixth month, an edict sent Erudites Chu Da, Xu Yan, and six others to tour the commanderies and kingdoms separately, reporting land-grabbers and guilty governors, chancellors, and officials.

sentences.zh: ----7秋，九月，冠軍景桓侯霍去病薨。

translations.literal: ----7 In autumn, the ninth month, Champion Marquis of Jinghuan Huo Qubing died.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In autumn, the ninth month, Champion Marquis of Jinghuan Huo Qubing died.

sentences.zh: 天子甚悼之，為塚，像祁連山。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven deeply mourned him, made his tomb, and shaped it like Mount Qilian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him, built his tomb, and shaped it like Mount Qilian.

sentences.zh: 初，霍仲孺吏畢歸家，娶婦，生子光。

translations.literal: At the outset, Huo Zhongru finished his service as a clerk and returned home, took a wife, and begot a son Guang.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Huo Zhongru finished his clerkship and returned home, took a wife, and begot a son named Guang.

sentences.zh: 去病既壯大，乃自知父為霍仲孺。

translations.literal: When Qubing had grown to manhood, he then knew for himself that his father was Huo Zhongru.
translations.idiomatic: When Qubing had grown to manhood, he learned that his father was Huo Zhongru.

sentences.zh: 會為驃騎將軍，擊匈奴，道出河東，遣吏迎仲孺而見之，大為買田宅奴婢而去；

translations.literal: It happened that he was Rapid Cavalry General striking the Xiongnu; his route passed through Hedong; he sent an officer to welcome Zhongru and met him, greatly buying fields, houses, and slave women for him and then departed;
translations.idiomatic: It happened that as Rapid Cavalry General he struck the Xiongnu; his route passed through Hedong; he sent an officer to welcome Zhongru and met him, bought him fields, houses, and slave women on a grand scale, and departed;

sentences.zh: 及還，因將光西至長安，任以為郎，稍遷至奉車都尉、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: when he returned he thereupon led Guang west to Chang'an, appointed him as a Gentleman, and gradually promoted him to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and Household Minister.
translations.idiomatic: on his return he led Guang west to Chang'an, appointed him Gentleman, and gradually promoted him to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and Household Minister.

sentences.zh: ----8是歲，大農令顏異誅。

translations.literal: ----8 That year, Grand Agriculture Minister Yan Yi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 That year, Grand Agriculture Minister Yan Yi was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，異以廉直，稍遷至九卿。

translations.literal: At the outset, Yi was upright and incorruptible and was gradually promoted to the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Yi was upright and incorruptible and was gradually promoted among the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 上與張湯既造白鹿皮幣，問異，異曰：「今王侯朝賀以蒼璧，直數千，而以皮薦反四十萬，本末不相稱。

translations.literal: After the emperor and Zhang Tang had created the white-deer-skin currency, they questioned Yi; Yi said: "Now when kings and marquises come to court with congratulations they present the dark jade disk, worth several thousand, yet the skin mat in return is forty thousand—root and branch do not match.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor and Zhang Tang created the white-deer-skin currency, they questioned Yi; Yi said, "When kings and marquises come to court they present the dark jade disk, worth several thousand, yet the skin mat in return is forty thousand—root and branch do not match.

sentences.zh: 」天子不說。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 張湯又與異有郤，及人有告異以它事，下張湯治異。

translations.literal: Zhang Tang also had a grudge against Yi; when someone reported Yi on another matter, the case was handed down to Zhang Tang to try Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tang also bore a grudge against Yi; when someone reported Yi on another matter, the case was handed to Zhang Tang.

sentences.zh: 異與客語初令下有不便者，異不應，微反脣。

translations.literal: Yi was speaking with a guest when a new edict came down with something inexpedient in it; Yi did not respond but slightly turned his lip.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was speaking with a guest when a new edict came down with something inexpedient in it; Yi did not respond but slightly curled his lip.

sentences.zh: 湯奏當：「異九卿，見令不便，不入言而腹誹，論死。

translations.literal: Tang memorialized for judgment: "Yi is among the Nine Ministers; seeing an edict inexpedient, he did not enter and speak but belly-slandered—sentence death.
translations.idiomatic: Tang memorialized for judgment, "Yi stands among the Nine Ministers; seeing an edict inexpedient, he did not speak up but belly-slandered—sentence death.

sentences.zh: 」自是之後，有腹誹之法比，而公卿大夫多諂諛取容矣。

translations.literal: " From this time forward there was a statute for belly-slander, and among high ministers and grandees many flattered and fawned for favor.
translations.idiomatic: " From this time forward there was a statute for belly-slander, and among high ministers and grandees many flattered and fawned for favor.

sentences.zh: 1夏，五月，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1. In summer, the fifth month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In summer, the fifth month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----2濟東王彭離驕悍，昏暮，與其奴、亡命少年數十人行剽殺人，取財物以為好，所殺發覺者百餘人，坐廢，徙上庸。

translations.literal: ----2 King Pengli of Jidong was arrogant and fierce; at dusk he went with his slaves and several dozen fugitive youths on raids to kill people, taking property for his pleasure; those killed who were discovered numbered more than a hundred—he was convicted, deposed, and moved to Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 King Pengli of Jidong was arrogant and fierce; at dusk he went with his slaves and several dozen fugitive youths on raids to kill and rob for pleasure; more than a hundred killings came to light—he was deposed and moved to Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十一月，張湯有罪自殺。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, Zhang Tang was guilty and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, Zhang Tang, found guilty, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 初，御史中丞李文，與湯有郤。

translations.literal: At the outset, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Wen had a grudge against Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Wen bore a grudge against Tang.

sentences.zh: 湯所厚吏魯謁居陰使人上變告文奸事，事下湯治，論殺之。

translations.literal: Lu Yeju, a clerk whom Tang favored, secretly had someone submit a report of change denouncing Wen for wicked affairs; the case was handed down to Tang for trial, and he sentenced Wen to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yeju, a clerk whom Tang favored, secretly had someone submit a denunciation of Wen for wicked affairs; Tang tried the case and sentenced Wen to death.

sentences.zh: 湯心知謁居為之，上問：「變事蹤跡安起？

translations.literal: Tang knew in his heart that Yeju had done it; the emperor asked: "Where did the trail of this report of change begin?
translations.idiomatic: Tang knew Yeju had done it; the emperor asked, "Where did the trail of this denunciation begin?

sentences.zh: 」湯佯驚曰：「此殆文故人怨之。

translations.literal: " Tang feigned alarm and said: "This is probably an old acquaintance of Wen bearing a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang feigned alarm and said, "This is probably some old acquaintance of Wen bearing a grudge.

sentences.zh: 」謁居病，湯親為之摩足。

translations.literal: " Yeju fell ill, and Tang personally massaged his feet for him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yeju fell ill, Tang personally massaged his feet.

sentences.zh: 趙王素怨湯，上書告：「湯大臣，乃與吏摩足，疑與為大奸。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao had long resented Tang and memorialized: "Tang is a great minister, yet he massages a clerk's feet—suspected of great wickedness together.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao had long resented Tang and memorialized, "Tang is a great minister, yet he massages a clerk's feet—suspected of great wickedness.

sentences.zh: 」事下廷尉。

translations.literal: " The affair was handed down to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " The affair was handed to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 謁居病死，事連其弟。

translations.literal: Yeju died of illness, and the affair connected to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yeju died of illness, and the affair connected to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 弟系導官，湯亦治他囚導官，見謁居弟，欲陰為之，而佯不省。

translations.literal: The younger brother was held at the Guide Office; Tang was also trying other prisoners at the Guide Office, saw Yeju's younger brother, wished secretly to help him, yet feigned not to recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother was held at the Guide Office; Tang was trying other prisoners there, saw Yeju's younger brother, wished secretly to help him, yet feigned not to know him.

sentences.zh: 謁居弟弗知，怨湯，使人上書，告湯與謁居謀共變告李文。

translations.literal: Yeju's younger brother did not know this, resented Tang, and had someone submit a memorial reporting that Tang and Yeju had plotted together to denounce Li Wen by report of change.
translations.idiomatic: Yeju's younger brother did not know this, resented Tang, and had someone memorialize that Tang and Yeju had plotted to denounce Li Wen.

sentences.zh: 事下減宣，宣嘗與湯有郤，及得此事，窮竟其事，未奏也。

translations.literal: The affair was handed down to Jian Xuan; Xuan had once had a grudge against Tang, and when he obtained this matter he exhaustively investigated it but had not yet memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The affair went to Jian Xuan; Xuan had once borne a grudge against Tang, and when he obtained the matter he investigated to the end but had not yet memorialized.

sentences.zh: 會人有盜發孝文園瘞錢，丞相青翟朝，與湯約俱謝，至前，湯獨不謝。

translations.literal: It happened that someone dug up and stole buried treasure from Emperor Wen's park; Chancellor Qingdi attended court, agreed with Tang to apologize together, but when they came before the throne Tang alone did not apologize.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that someone dug up buried treasure from Emperor Wen's park; Chancellor Qingdi attended court and agreed with Tang to apologize together, but at the throne Tang alone did not apologize.

sentences.zh: 上使御史案丞相，湯欲致其文「丞相見知」，丞相患之。

translations.literal: The emperor had the censor investigate the chancellor; Tang wished to bring a charge of "the chancellor knew and connived," and the chancellor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the censor investigate the chancellor; Tang wished to bring a charge that "the chancellor knew and connived," and the chancellor was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 丞相長史朱買臣、王朝、邊通，皆故九卿、二千石，仕宦絕在湯前。

translations.literal: The chancellor's chief clerks Zhu Maichen, Wang Chao, and Bian Tong were all former Nine Ministers and officials at the two-thousand-bushel rank whose careers entirely preceded Tang's.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's chief clerks Zhu Maichen, Wang Chao, and Bian Tong were all former Nine Ministers and two-thousand-bushel officials whose careers entirely preceded Tang's.

sentences.zh: 湯數行丞相事，知三長史素貴，故陵折，丞史遇之，三長史皆怨恨，欲死之。

translations.literal: Tang repeatedly acted in chancellor affairs, knew the three chief clerks were by nature honored, and therefore humbled and bent them; when the chancellor's clerks met them, all three chief clerks resented him and wished him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Tang repeatedly acted in chancellor affairs, knew the three chief clerks were by nature proud, and therefore humbled them; all three resented him and wished him dead.

sentences.zh: 乃與丞相謀，使吏捕案賈人田信等，曰：「湯且欲奏請，信輒先知之，居物致富，與湯分之。

translations.literal: They thereupon plotted with the chancellor, had officers arrest and try the merchant Tian Xin and others, and said: "Whenever Tang was about to memorialize a request, Xin always knew it beforehand, hoarded goods and grew rich, and divided with Tang.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted with the chancellor, had officers arrest the merchant Tian Xin and others, and said, "Whenever Tang was about to memorialize a request, Xin always knew beforehand, hoarded goods and grew rich, and divided the profit with Tang.

sentences.zh: 」事辭頗聞，上問湯曰：「吾所為，賈人輒先知之，益居其物，是類有以吾謀告之者。

translations.literal: " The words of the case became somewhat known; the emperor asked Tang: "What I do, the merchants always know beforehand and further hoard its goods—this is like someone reporting my plans to them.
translations.idiomatic: " Word of the case spread; the emperor asked Tang, "Whatever I do, the merchants always know beforehand and hoard the goods—this is as if someone were reporting my plans to them.

sentences.zh: 」湯不謝，又佯驚曰：「固宜有。

translations.literal: " Tang did not apologize but again feigned alarm and said: "Of course there should be.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang did not apologize but again feigned alarm and said, "Of course there should be.

sentences.zh: 」減宣亦奏謁居等事。

translations.literal: " Jian Xuan also memorialized on Yeju and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian Xuan also memorialized on Yeju and the rest.

sentences.zh: 天子以湯懷詐面欺，使趙禹切責湯，湯乃為書謝，因曰：「陷臣者，三長史也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven regarded Tang as harboring deceit and facing him with fraud, sent Zhao Yu to rebuke him sharply, and Tang thereupon wrote a letter of apology, saying therein: "Those who trapped your servant are the three chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Tang as harboring deceit and facing him with fraud, sent Zhao Yu to rebuke him sharply, and Tang wrote a letter of apology, saying, "Those who trapped me are the three chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: " He thereupon committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon took his own life.

sentences.zh: 湯既死，家產直不過五百金。

translations.literal: After Tang died, the worth of his household goods did not exceed five hundred in gold.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang died, his household goods were worth no more than five hundred in gold.

sentences.zh: 昆弟諸子欲厚葬湯，湯母曰：「湯為天子大臣，被污惡言而死，何厚葬乎！

translations.literal: His brothers and sons wished to bury Tang lavishly; Tang's mother said: "Tang was a great minister of the Son of Heaven, died under filthy and wicked words—why bury him lavishly!
translations.idiomatic: His brothers and sons wished to bury him lavishly; Tang's mother said, "Tang was a great minister of the Son of Heaven and died under filthy accusations—why bury him lavishly!

sentences.zh: 」載以牛車，有棺無槨。

translations.literal: " He was carried on an ox cart, with a coffin but no outer coffin.
translations.idiomatic: " He was carried on an ox cart, with a coffin but no outer case.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之，乃盡按誅三長史。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard this, he thereupon fully investigated and executed the three chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he fully investigated and executed the three chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬辰，丞相青翟下獄，自殺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Chancellor Qingdi was placed in prison and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Chancellor Qingdi was imprisoned and took his own life.

sentences.zh: ----2春，起柏梁台。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the Bolang Terrace was begun.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, work began on the Bolang Terrace.

sentences.zh: 作承露盤，高二十丈，大七圍，以銅為之。

translations.literal: The Dew-Receiving Basin was made, twenty zhang high and seven arm-spans around, cast of bronze.
translations.idiomatic: They made the Dew-Receiving Basin, twenty zhang high and seven arm-spans around, cast of bronze.

sentences.zh: 上有仙人掌，以承露，和玉屑飲之，雲可以長生。

translations.literal: Upon it was a cactus pillar to receive dew; mixed with jade powder and drunk, it was said one could attain long life.
translations.idiomatic: Upon it stood a cactus pillar to catch dew; mixed with powdered jade and drunk, it was said to grant long life.

sentences.zh: 宮室之修，自此日盛。

translations.literal: The ornamentation of palaces and halls from this day grew daily more lavish.
translations.idiomatic: From this day the ornamentation of palaces grew ever more lavish.

sentences.zh: ----3二月，以太子太傅趙周為丞相。

translations.literal: ----3 In the second month, the Heir Apparent's Grand Tutor Zhao Zhou was made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the second month, Heir Apparent's Grand Tutor Zhao Zhou was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----4三月，辛亥，以太子太傅石慶為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----4 In the third month, on xinhai, the Heir Apparent's Grand Tutor Shi Qing was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the third month, on xinhai, Heir Apparent's Grand Tutor Shi Qing was made Censor-in-Chief.

translations.literal: ----5 There was heavy rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 There was heavy rain and snow.

sentences.zh: ----6夏，大水，關東餓死者以千數。

translations.literal: ----6 In summer there were great floods; east of the passes those who starved to death numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In summer came great floods; east of the passes the starving dead numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: ----7是歲，孔僅為大農令，而桑弘羊為大農中丞，稍置均輸，以通貨物。

translations.literal: ----7 That year, Kong Jin was Grand Agriculture Minister and Sang Hongyang was Vice Grand Agriculture Minister; they gradually established equalizing transport to circulate goods.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 That year Kong Jin was Grand Agriculture Minister and Sang Hongyang Vice Minister; they gradually established equalizing transport to circulate goods.

sentences.zh: ----8白金稍賤，民不寶用，竟廢之。

translations.literal: ----8 White metal gradually fell in value; the people did not treasure and use it, and in the end it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 White metal gradually fell in value; the people would not treasure it, and in the end it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 於是悉禁郡、國無鑄錢，專令上林三官鑄錢，令天下非三官錢不得行。

translations.literal: Thereupon casting coin in commanderies and kingdoms was entirely forbidden; casting was entrusted solely to the Three Offices of Shanglin, and an edict ordered that under Heaven no coin but that of the Three Offices might circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon coinage in commanderies and kingdoms was forbidden entirely; only the Three Offices of Shanglin might cast coin, and no other coin might circulate under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 而民之鑄錢益少，計其費不能相當。

translations.literal: Yet the people's coin-casting grew ever fewer; reckoning the cost, it could not balance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people cast ever less coin; reckoning the cost, it could not balance.

sentences.zh: 惟真工、大奸乃盜為之。

translations.literal: Only true craftsmen and great villains secretly made it.
translations.idiomatic: Only skilled craftsmen and great villains counterfeited it in secret.

sentences.zh: ----9渾邪王既降漢，漢兵擊逐匈奴於幕北，自鹽澤以東空無匈奴，西域道可通。

translations.literal: ----9 Once the King of Hunye had surrendered to Han, Han troops attacked and drove the Xiongnu north of the desert curtain; from the Salt Marsh eastward there were no Xiongnu, and the Western Regions road could be opened.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 Once the King of Hunye had surrendered to Han, Han troops attacked and drove the Xiongnu north of the desert curtain; from the Salt Marsh eastward the land was empty of Xiongnu, and the road to the Western Regions could be opened.

sentences.zh: 於是張騫建言：「烏孫王昆莫本為匈奴臣，後兵稍強，不肯復朝事匈奴，匈奴攻不勝而遠之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Qian offered counsel: "The King of Wusun Kunmo was originally a subject of the Xiongnu; later his troops grew somewhat strong, and he refused again to attend court and serve the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu attacked but could not overcome him and distanced themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhang Qian offered counsel, saying, "The King of Wusun, Kunmo, was originally a subject of the Xiongnu; later his forces grew somewhat strong, and he refused again to attend court and serve the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu attacked but could not overcome him and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 今單于新困於漢，而故渾邪地空無人，蠻夷俗戀故地，又貪漢財物，今誠以此時厚幣賂烏孫，招以益東，居故渾邪之地，與漢結昆弟，其勢宜聽，聽則是斷匈奴右臂也。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu is newly distressed by Han, while the former Hunye lands are empty and without people; barbarian custom clings to old lands, and they also covet Han goods; if we truly at this time richly bribe Wusun with gifts and summon them to move further east to dwell in the former Hunye lands, forming brotherhood with Han—the situation ought to make them listen; if they listen, that is cutting off the Xiongnu's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu is newly hard pressed by Han, while the former Hunye lands lie empty; barbarians by custom cling to old lands and also covet Han goods. If we truly at this time richly bribe Wusun and summon them to move further east to dwell in the former Hunye lands, forming brotherhood with Han, they ought to listen; if they listen, that is cutting off the Xiongnu's right arm.

sentences.zh: 既連烏孫，自其西大夏之屬皆可招來而為外臣。

translations.literal: Once Wusun is linked, from their west all such states as Daxia can be summoned to come and become outer subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wusun is linked, from their west all such states as Daxia can be summoned to come and become outer subjects.

sentences.zh: 」天子以為然，拜騫為中郎將，將三百人，馬各二匹，牛羊以萬數，繼金幣帛直數千巨萬；

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven thought it correct, invested Qian as Palace Gentleman-General, led three hundred men, each with two horses, cattle and sheep in tens of thousands, and gifts of gold, coins, and silks worth several thousand times ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thought it correct, invested Qian as Palace Gentleman-General, led three hundred men, each with two horses, cattle and sheep in tens of thousands, and gifts of gold, coins, and silks worth several thousand times ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 多持節副使，道可便，遣之他旁國。

translations.literal: many bore credentials as deputy envoys; where the road was convenient, he dispatched them to other neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: many bore credentials as deputy envoys; where the road was convenient, he dispatched them to other neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 騫既至烏孫，昆莫見騫，禮節甚倨。

translations.literal: Once Qian had reached Wusun, Kunmo received Qian with ceremony very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qian had reached Wusun, Kunmo received him with very arrogant ceremony.

sentences.zh: 騫諭指曰：「烏孫能東居故地，則漢遣公主為夫人，結為兄弟，共距匈奴，匈奴不足破也。

translations.literal: Qian expounded the intent, saying: "If Wusun can move east to dwell in the old lands, Han will send a princess as consort, form brotherhood, and together resist the Xiongnu—the Xiongnu are not worth breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Qian expounded the intent, saying, "If Wusun can move east to dwell in the old lands, Han will send a princess as consort, form brotherhood, and together resist the Xiongnu—the Xiongnu are not hard to break.

sentences.zh: 」烏孫自以遠漢，未知其大小；

translations.literal: " Wusun on their own considered themselves far from Han and did not know its size;
translations.idiomatic: " Wusun on their own considered themselves far from Han and did not know its size;

sentences.zh: 素服屬匈奴日久，且又近之，其大臣皆畏匈奴，不欲移徙。

translations.literal: having long submitted and belonged to the Xiongnu, and being moreover near them, their great ministers all feared the Xiongnu and did not wish to relocate.
translations.idiomatic: having long submitted to the Xiongnu, and being moreover near them, their great ministers all feared the Xiongnu and did not wish to relocate.

sentences.zh: 騫留久之，不能得其要領，因分遣副使使大宛、康居、大月氏、大夏、安息、身毒、于闐及諸旁國，烏孫發譯道送騫還，使數十人，馬數十匹，隨騫報謝，因令窺漢大小。

translations.literal: Qian stayed long but could not obtain their essentials; he therefore separately dispatched deputy envoys to Dayuan, Kangju, the Great Yuezhi, Daxia, Parthia, Shendu, Yutian, and various neighboring states; Wusun sent interpreters along the road to escort Qian back, with several tens of men and several tens of horses following Qian to return thanks, and thereby to spy out Han's size.
translations.idiomatic: Qian stayed long but could not obtain their essentials; he therefore separately dispatched deputy envoys to Dayuan, Kangju, the Great Yuezhi, Daxia, Parthia, Shendu, Yutian, and various neighboring states; Wusun sent interpreters along the road to escort Qian back, with several tens of men and several tens of horses following him to return thanks and thereby spy out Han's size.

sentences.zh: 是歲，騫還，到，拜為大行。

translations.literal: That year Qian returned; upon arrival he was invested as Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qian returned; upon arrival he was invested as Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，騫所遣使通大夏之屬者，皆頗與其人俱來，於是西域始通於漢矣。

translations.literal: More than a year later, the envoys Qian had sent who had reached Daxia and the like all largely came back together with men of those lands; thereupon the Western Regions first opened communication with Han.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, the envoys Qian had sent who had reached Daxia and the like all largely came back together with men of those lands; thereupon the Western Regions first opened communication with Han.

sentences.zh: 西域凡三十六國，南北有大山，中央有河，東西六千餘里，南北千餘里，東則接漢玉門、陽關，西則限以蔥嶺。

translations.literal: The Western Regions in all had thirty-six states; north and south were great mountains, in the center a river; east-west more than six thousand li, north-south more than a thousand li; east they adjoined Han's Jade Gate and Yang Pass, west they were bounded by the Onion Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions in all had thirty-six states; great mountains lay north and south, with a river in the center; east-west more than six thousand li, north-south more than a thousand li; east they adjoined Han's Jade Gate and Yang Pass, west they were bounded by the Onion Mountains.

sentences.zh: 河有兩源，一出蔥嶺，一出于闐，合流東注鹽澤。

translations.literal: The river had two sources: one issued from the Onion Mountains, one from Yutian; joining they flowed east and poured into the Salt Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The river had two sources: one issued from the Onion Mountains, one from Yutian; joining they flowed east and poured into the Salt Marsh.

sentences.zh: 鹽澤去玉門、陽關三百餘里。

translations.literal: The Salt Marsh was more than three hundred li from the Jade Gate and Yang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt Marsh was more than three hundred li from the Jade Gate and Yang Pass.

sentences.zh: 自玉門、陽關出西域有兩道：從鄯善傍南山北，循河西行至莎車，為南道；

translations.literal: From the Jade Gate and Yang Pass out into the Western Regions there were two routes: from Shanshan along the north of the southern mountains, following the river west to reach Yarkand—this was the southern route;
translations.idiomatic: From the Jade Gate and Yang Pass out into the Western Regions there were two routes: from Shanshan along the north of the southern mountains, following the river west to Yarkand—this was the southern route;

sentences.zh: 南道西逾蔥嶺，則出大月氏、安息。

translations.literal: the southern route west crossing the Onion Mountains then issued toward the Great Yuezhi and Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: the southern route, crossing the Onion Mountains westward, issued toward the Great Yuezhi and Parthia.

sentences.zh: 自車師前王廷隨北山循河西行至疏勒，為北道；

translations.literal: From the court of the Former King of Cheshi, following the northern mountains along the river west to Kashgar—this was the northern route;
translations.idiomatic: From the court of the Former King of Cheshi, following the northern mountains along the river west to Kashgar—this was the northern route;

sentences.zh: 北道西逾蔥嶺，則出大宛、康居、奄蔡焉。

translations.literal: the northern route west crossing the Onion Mountains then issued toward Dayuan, Kangju, and Aorsi.
translations.idiomatic: the northern route, crossing the Onion Mountains westward, issued toward Dayuan, Kangju, and Aorsi.

sentences.zh: 故皆役屬匈奴，匈奴西邊日逐王，置僮僕都尉，使領西域，常居焉耆、危須、尉黎間，賦稅諸國，取富給焉。

translations.literal: Formerly all were subject and subordinate to the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu western-border Ri-zhu King established the Tongpu Commandant to lead the Western Regions, regularly dwelling among Yanqi, Weixu, and Weili, levying taxes on the states and taking wealth to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly all were subject to the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu western-border Ri-zhu King established the Tongpu Commandant to lead the Western Regions, regularly dwelling among Yanqi, Weixu, and Weili, levying taxes on the states and taking wealth to supply himself.

sentences.zh: 烏孫王既不肯東還，漢乃於渾邪王故地置酒泉郡，稍發徙民以充實之；

translations.literal: Since the King of Wusun would not move east and return, Han thereupon established Jiuquan commandery on the former Hunye lands and gradually dispatched relocated people to fill it;
translations.idiomatic: Since the King of Wusun would not move east and return, Han thereupon established Jiuquan commandery on the former Hunye lands and gradually dispatched relocated people to fill it;

sentences.zh: 後又分置武威郡，以絕匈奴與羌通之道。

translations.literal: later they also separately established Wuwei commandery to cut off the road by which the Xiongnu communicated with the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: later they also separately established Wuwei commandery to cut off the road by which the Xiongnu communicated with the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天子得宛汗血馬，愛之，名曰「天馬」。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven obtained Ferghana sweat-blood horses, loved them, and named them "Heavenly Horses."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor obtained Ferghana sweat-blood horses, loved them, and named them "Heavenly Horses."

sentences.zh: 使者相望於道以求之。

translations.literal: Envoys lined the road one after another seeking them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys lined the road one after another seeking them.

sentences.zh: 諸使外國，一輩大者數百，少者百餘人，人所賫操大放博望侯時，其後益習而衰少焉。

translations.literal: Envoys to foreign states: one mission large ones numbered several hundred, small ones a hundred-odd men; what each person carried and held was far greater than in the Marquis of Bowang's time—afterward they grew more practiced and diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to foreign states: the large missions numbered several hundred, the small over a hundred men; what each person carried was far greater than in the Marquis of Bowang's time—afterward they grew more practiced and the scale diminished.

sentences.zh: 漢率一歲中使多者十餘，少者五六輩；

translations.literal: Han on average in one year sent out at most over ten missions, at least five or six;
translations.idiomatic: Han on average in one year sent out at most over ten missions, at least five or six;

sentences.zh: 遠者八九歲，近者數歲而反。

translations.literal: the far ones eight or nine years, the near ones several years before returning.
translations.idiomatic: the far ones eight or nine years, the near ones several years before returning.

sentences.zh: 1冬，徙函谷關於新安。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, Hangu Pass was moved to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, Hangu Pass was moved to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: ----2春，正月，戊子，陽陵園火。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the first month, on wuzi, the Yangling park burned.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the first month, on wuzi, the Yangling park burned.

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, hail fell.

sentences.zh: ----4關東郡、國十餘饑，人相食。

translations.literal: ----4 More than ten commanderies and kingdoms east of the passes suffered famine; people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 More than ten commanderies and kingdoms east of the passes suffered famine; people ate one another.

sentences.zh: ----5常山憲王舜薨，子勃嗣，坐憲王病不侍疾，及居喪無禮廢，徙房陵。

translations.literal: ----5 King Xian of Changshan Shun died; his son Bo succeeded, was convicted for not attending his father King Xian in illness and for lacking mourning rites while in mourning, was deposed, and was relocated to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 King Xian of Changshan Shun died; his son Bo succeeded, was convicted for not attending his father in illness and for lacking mourning rites, was deposed, and relocated to Fangling.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，天子更封憲王子平為真定王，以常山為郡，於是五嶽皆在天子之邦矣。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the Son of Heaven again enfeoffed King Xian's son Ping as King of Zhending and made Changshan a commandery; thereupon all five sacred peaks were within the Son of Heaven's domain.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, the emperor again enfeoffed King Xian's son Ping as King of Zhending and made Changshan a commandery; thereupon all five sacred peaks lay within the emperor's domain.

sentences.zh: ----6徙代王義為清河王。

translations.literal: ----6 The Prince of Dai Yi was transferred to be Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 The Prince of Dai Yi was transferred to be Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: ----7是歲，匈奴伊稚斜單于死，子烏維單于立。

translations.literal: ----7 That year the Xiongnu Chanyu Yizhixie died; his son Wuwu was established as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 That year the Xiongnu Chanyu Yizhixie died; his son Wuwu was established as Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上行幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今上帝，朕親郊，而-{后土}-無祀，則禮不答也，其令有司議。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Now for the Supreme Lord, I personally perform suburban sacrifice, yet -{后土}- has no sacrifice—then the rites do not respond; let the responsible offices deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Now for the Supreme Lord I personally perform suburban sacrifice, yet -{后土}- has no sacrifice—then the rites do not respond; let the responsible offices deliberate.

sentences.zh: 」立-{后土}-祠於澤中圜丘。

translations.literal: " An altar to -{后土}- was established at the round mound in the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: " An altar to -{后土}- was established at the round mound in the marsh.

sentences.zh: 上遂自夏陽東幸汾陰。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon from Xiayang traveled in favor east to Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon traveled in favor east from Xiayang to Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 是時，天子始巡郡、國。

translations.literal: At this time the Son of Heaven first toured the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor first toured the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 河東守不意行至，不辦，自殺。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Hedong, not expecting the emperor's arrival, was unprepared and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Hedong, not expecting the emperor's arrival, was unprepared and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子，立-{后土}-祠於汾陰脽上，上親望拜，如上帝禮，禮畢，行幸滎陽，還，至洛陽，封周後姬嘉為周子南君。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, an altar to -{后土}- was established on the Fenyin mound; the emperor personally gazed and bowed, as with the Supreme Lord's rites; when the rites were complete, he traveled in favor to Xingyang, returned, reached Luoyang, and enfeoffed Ji Jia, descendant of Zhou, as Lord of Zhouzi South.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, an altar to -{后土}- was established on the Fenyin mound; the emperor personally gazed and bowed, as with the Supreme Lord's rites; when the rites were complete, he traveled in favor to Xingyang, returned, reached Luoyang, and enfeoffed Ji Jia, descendant of Zhou, as Lord of Zhouzi South.

sentences.zh: ----2春，二月，中山靖王勝薨。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the second month, King Jing of Zhongshan Sheng died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the second month, King Jing of Zhongshan Sheng died.

sentences.zh: ----3樂成侯丁義薦方士欒大，云與文成將軍同師。

translations.literal: ----3 Marquis of Lecheng Ding Yi recommended the method master Luan Da, saying he shared a teacher with General Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Marquis of Lecheng Ding Yi recommended the method master Luan Da, saying he shared a teacher with General Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 上方悔誅文成，得欒大，大說。

translations.literal: The emperor above was repenting having executed Wencheng; obtaining Luan Da, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was repenting having executed Wencheng; obtaining Luan Da, he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 大先事膠東康王，為人長美言，多方略，而敢為大言，處之不疑。

translations.literal: Da had first served King Kang of Jiaodong; as a man he was tall and fair-spoken, with many stratagems, and dared speak grandly, placing himself in it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Da had first served King Kang of Jiaodong; he was tall and fair-spoken, with many stratagems, dared speak grandly, and placed himself in it without doubt.

sentences.zh: 大言曰：「臣常往來海中，見安期、羨門之屬，顧以臣為賤，不信臣；

translations.literal: Da spoke grandly, saying: "Your servant often goes back and forth on the sea and has seen Anqi, Xianmen, and the like; they only regard your servant as base and do not trust him;
translations.idiomatic: Da spoke grandly, saying, "Your servant often goes back and forth on the sea and has seen Anqi, Xianmen, and the like; they only regard me as base and do not trust me;

sentences.zh: 又以為康王諸侯耳，不足與方。

translations.literal: they also consider the King of Jiaodong a mere feudal lord, not worth sharing methods with.
translations.idiomatic: they also consider the King of Jiaodong a mere feudal lord, not worth sharing methods with.

sentences.zh: 臣之師曰：『黃金可成而河決可塞，不死之藥可得，仙人可致也。

translations.literal: Your servant's teacher said: 'Gold can be perfected and the Yellow River's breach can be stopped; the drug of non-death can be obtained; immortals can be summoned.'
translations.idiomatic: My teacher said, 'Gold can be perfected and the Yellow River's breach can be stopped; the drug of immortality can be obtained; immortals can be summoned.'

sentences.zh: 』然臣恐效文成，則方士皆掩口，惡敢言方哉！

translations.literal: ' Yet your servant fears that if he follows Wencheng's example, then all method masters will cover their mouths—how dare they speak of methods!
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet I fear that if I follow Wencheng's example, then all method masters will cover their mouths—how dare they speak of methods!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「文成食馬肝死耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Wencheng died from eating horse liver, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Wencheng died from eating horse liver, that's all.

sentences.zh: 子誠能修其方，我何愛乎！

translations.literal: If you truly can practice his methods, what would I begrudge!
translations.idiomatic: If you truly can practice his methods, what would I begrudge!

sentences.zh: 」大曰：「臣師非有求人，人者求之。

translations.literal: " Da said: "Your servant's teacher does not seek people—people seek him.
translations.idiomatic: " Da said, "My teacher does not seek people—people seek him.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲致之，則貴其使者，令為親屬，以客禮待之，乃可使通言於神人。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must summon him, then honor his envoy, make him kin, treat him with guest ceremony—only then can one have words passed to the divine man.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must summon him, then honor his envoy, make him kin, treat him with guest ceremony—only then can one have words passed to the divine man.

sentences.zh: 」於是上使驗小方，斗旗，旗自相觸擊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor had a small method tested: battling flags—the flags struck one another of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the emperor had a small method tested: battling flags—the flags struck one another of themselves.

sentences.zh: 是時，上方憂河決而黃金不就，乃拜大為五利將軍，又拜為天士將軍，地士將軍，大通將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor above was anxious over the Yellow River's breach and gold not being perfected; he thereupon invested Da as General of Five Benefits, and also as General of the Heaven Soldier, General of the Earth Soldier, and General of Great Communication.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was anxious over the Yellow River's breach and gold not being perfected; he thereupon invested Da as General of Five Benefits, and also as General of the Heaven Soldier, General of the Earth Soldier, and General of Great Communication.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙巳，封大為樂通侯，食邑二千戶，賜甲第，僮千人，乘輿斥車馬、帷帳、器物以充其家，又以衛長公主妻之，賫金十萬斤，天子親如五利之第，使者存問共給，相屬於道。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, Da was enfeoffed as Marquis of Letong with a fief of two thousand households, granted a mansion of the first rank, a thousand household slaves, imperial escort carriages, horses, curtains, and utensils to fill his house; moreover the Eldest Princess of Wei was given him as wife, with a dowry of a hundred thousand jin of gold; the Son of Heaven personally went to the Marquis of Five Benefits' residence; envoys called to inquire and jointly supplied him, one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, Da was enfeoffed as Marquis of Letong with a fief of two thousand households, granted a mansion of the first rank, a thousand household slaves, imperial escort carriages, horses, curtains, and utensils to fill his house; moreover the Eldest Princess of Wei was given him as wife, with a dowry of a hundred thousand jin of gold; the emperor personally went to the Marquis of Five Benefits' residence; envoys called to inquire and jointly supplied him, one after another on the road.

sentences.zh: 自太主、將、相以下，皆置酒其家，獻遺之。

translations.literal: From the Eldest Princess, generals, and chancellors down, all set out wine at his house and presented gifts to him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eldest Princess, generals, and chancellors down, all set out wine at his house and presented gifts to him.

sentences.zh: 天子又刻玉印曰「天道將軍」，使使衣羽衣，夜立白茅上；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also carved a jade seal reading "General of Heaven's Way," had an envoy wear feather robes and stand on white thatch by night;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also carved a jade seal reading "General of Heaven's Way," had an envoy wear feather robes and stand on white thatch by night;

sentences.zh: 五利將軍亦衣羽衣，立白茅上，受印，以示不臣。

translations.literal: the General of Five Benefits also wore feather robes, stood on white thatch, received the seal, to show he was not a subject.
translations.idiomatic: the General of Five Benefits also wore feather robes, stood on white thatch, received the seal, to show he was not a subject.

sentences.zh: 大見數月，佩六印，貴震天下。

translations.literal: Within several months after Da was received, he wore six seals; his nobility shook all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Within several months after Da was received, he wore six seals; his nobility shook all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 於是海上燕、齊之間，莫不扼腕自言有禁方、能神仙矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon between Yan and Qi along the seacoast, none failed to clench their wrists and declare on their own that they had secret formulas and could become immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon along the seacoast between Yan and Qi, none failed to clench their wrists and declare that they had secret formulas and could become immortals.

sentences.zh: ----4六月，汾陰巫錦得大鼎於魏脽后土營旁，河東太守以聞。

translations.literal: ----4 In the sixth month, the Fenyin shaman Jin obtained a great ding beside the Wei mound's -{后土}- camp; the Administrator of Hedong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the sixth month, the Fenyin shaman Jin obtained a great ding beside the Wei mound's -{后土}- camp; the Administrator of Hedong reported it.

sentences.zh: 天子使驗問，巫得鼎無奸詐，乃以禮祠，迎鼎至甘泉，從上行，薦之宗廟及上帝，藏於甘泉宮，群臣皆上壽賀。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent men to examine and question; the shaman's obtaining the ding involved no deceit; he thereupon sacrificed it by rite, welcomed the ding to Ganquan, followed the emperor on the journey, presented it to the ancestral temple and the Supreme Lord, stored it in Ganquan Palace, and all the ministers offered longevity congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to examine and question; the shaman's obtaining the ding involved no deceit; he thereupon sacrificed it by rite, welcomed the ding to Ganquan, followed the emperor on the journey, presented it to the ancestral temple and the Supreme Lord, stored it in Ganquan Palace, and all the ministers offered longevity congratulations.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，立常山憲王子商為泗水王。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, King Xian of Changshan's son Shang was established as King of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, King Xian of Changshan's son Shang was established as King of Sishui.

sentences.zh: ----6初，條侯周亞夫為丞相，趙禹為丞相史，府中皆稱其廉平，然亞夫弗任，曰：「極知禹無害，然文深，不可以居大府。

translations.literal: ----6 At the outset, when Marquis of Tiao Zhou Yafu was Chancellor, Zhao Yu was Chancellor's Clerk; within the office all praised him as incorrupt and fair, yet Yafu did not employ him, saying: "I fully know Yu is harmless, yet he is deep in paperwork and cannot dwell in the great office.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 At the outset, when Marquis of Tiao Zhou Yafu was Chancellor, Zhao Yu was Chancellor's Clerk; within the office all praised him as incorrupt and fair, yet Yafu did not employ him, saying, "I fully know Yu is harmless, yet he is deep in paperwork and cannot dwell in the great office.

sentences.zh: 」及禹為少府，比九卿為酷急；

translations.literal: " When Yu became Minister of the Privy Purse, compared with the Nine Ministers he was harsh and urgent;
translations.idiomatic: " When Yu became Minister of the Privy Purse, compared with the Nine Ministers he was harsh and urgent;

sentences.zh: 至晚節，吏務為嚴峻，而禹更名寬平。

translations.literal: by his late years clerks strove to be stern and severe, while Yu changed his name to Kuanping.
translations.idiomatic: by his late years clerks strove to be stern and severe, while Yu changed his name to Kuanping.

sentences.zh: 中尉尹齊素以敢斬伐著名，及為中尉，吏民益凋敝。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Yin Qi was by nature famed for daring execution and cutting down; once he became Commandant of the Guards, officials and people grew ever more wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Yin Qi was famed for daring execution and cutting down; once he became Commandant of the Guards, officials and people grew ever more wasted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊坐不勝任抵罪。

translations.literal: That year Qi was convicted for incompetence and punished.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi was convicted for incompetence and punished.

sentences.zh: 上乃復以王溫舒為中尉，趙禹為廷尉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon again made Wang Wenshu Commandant of the Guards and Zhao Yu Court Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon again made Wang Wenshu Commandant of the Guards and Zhao Yu Court Commandant.

sentences.zh: 後四年，禹以老，貶為燕相。

translations.literal: Four years later Yu, on account of age, was demoted to Chancellor of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Yu, on account of age, was demoted to Chancellor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 是時吏治以慘刻相尚，獨左內史兒寬，勸農業，緩刑罰，理獄訟，務在得人心；

translations.literal: At that time official governance took cruel severity as fashion; only Left Metropolitan Steward Er Kuan urged agriculture, eased punishments, judged prison cases, and strove to win people's hearts;
translations.idiomatic: At that time official governance prized cruel severity; only Left Metropolitan Steward Er Kuan urged agriculture, eased punishments, judged prison cases, and strove to win people's hearts;

sentences.zh: 擇用仁厚士，推情與下，不求名聲，吏民大信愛之；

translations.literal: he chose and employed benevolent, generous men, extended feeling to those below, did not seek reputation, and officials and people greatly trusted and loved him;
translations.idiomatic: he chose and employed benevolent, generous men, extended feeling to those below, did not seek reputation, and officials and people greatly trusted and loved him;

sentences.zh: 收租稅時，裁闊狹，與民相假貸，以故租多不入。

translations.literal: when collecting rent and tax he judged wide or narrow, lent to the people mutually, and for this reason much rent did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: when collecting rent and tax he judged wide or narrow, lent to the people, and for this reason much rent did not enter.

sentences.zh: 後有軍發，左內史以負租課殿，當免；

translations.literal: Later when troops were raised, the Left Metropolitan Steward because of deficient rent was ranked last in assessment and ought to be dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Later when troops were raised, the Left Metropolitan Steward because of deficient rent was ranked last in assessment and ought to be dismissed;

sentences.zh: 民聞當免，皆恐失之，大家牛車、小家擔負輸租，繈屬不絕，課更以最。

translations.literal: when the people heard he was to be dismissed, all feared losing him; great households used ox-carts, small households shouldered burdens to deliver rent, infants in succession without end, and in assessment he again ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: when the people heard he was to be dismissed, all feared losing him; great households used ox-carts, small households shouldered burdens to deliver rent, infants in succession without end, and in assessment he again ranked first.

sentences.zh: 上由此愈奇寬。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby grew ever more struck by Kuan's wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereby grew ever more impressed by Kuan.

sentences.zh: ----7初，南越文王遣其子嬰齊入宿衛，在長安取邯鄲樛氏女，生子興。

translations.literal: ----7 At the outset, King Wen of Southern Yue sent his son Yingqi to enter palace guard service; in Chang'an he took as wife a lady of the Jiao clan of Handan and fathered Xing.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 At the outset, King Wen of Southern Yue sent his son Yingqi to enter palace guard service; in Chang'an he took as wife a lady of the Jiao clan of Handan and fathered Xing.

sentences.zh: 文王薨，嬰齊立，乃藏其先武帝璽，上書請立樛氏女為后，興為嗣。

translations.literal: When King Wen died, Yingqi succeeded; he then hid his forebear's Emperor Wu seal, memorialized requesting that the lady of the Jiao clan be established as queen and Xing as heir.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen died, Yingqi succeeded; he then hid his forebear's Emperor Wu seal, memorialized requesting that the lady of the Jiao clan be established as queen and Xing as heir.

sentences.zh: 漢數使使者風諭嬰齊入朝。

translations.literal: Han repeatedly sent envoys to admonish and instruct Yingqi to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Han repeatedly sent envoys to admonish Yingqi to enter court.

sentences.zh: 嬰齊尚樂擅殺生自恣，懼入見要，用漢法比內諸侯，固稱病，遂不入見。

translations.literal: Yingqi still delighted in arbitrary killing for his own pleasure, feared that entering audience would bring demands to be judged by Han law like inner feudal lords, firmly claimed illness, and thus did not enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi still delighted in arbitrary killing for his own pleasure, feared that entering audience would bring demands to be judged by Han law like inner feudal lords, firmly claimed illness, and thus did not enter audience.

sentences.zh: 嬰齊薨，謚曰明王。

translations.literal: When Yingqi died, his posthumous title was King Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingqi died, his posthumous title was King Ming.

sentences.zh: 太子興代立，其母為太后。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xing succeeded in his place; his mother became Queen Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xing succeeded in his place; his mother became Queen Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后自未為嬰齊姬時，嘗與霸陵人安國少季通。

translations.literal: The Queen Dowager, before she became Yingqi's consort, had once been intimate with Anguo Shaoji of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: The Queen Dowager, before she became Yingqi's consort, had once been intimate with Anguo Shaoji of Baling.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上使安國少季往諭王、王太后以入朝，比內諸侯，令辯士諫大夫終軍等宣其辭，勇士魏臣等輔其決，衛尉路博德將兵屯桂陽待使者。

translations.literal: That year the emperor sent Anguo Shaoji to instruct the king and Queen Dowager to enter court, comparable to inner feudal lords; he ordered persuasive scholars Remonstrating Grandee Zhong Jun and others to proclaim the words, brave men Wei Chen and others to assist the decision, and Commandant of the Guard Lu Bode to lead troops and encamp at Guiyang awaiting the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor sent Anguo Shaoji to instruct the king and Queen Dowager to enter court, comparable to inner feudal lords; he ordered persuasive scholars Remonstrating Grandee Zhong Jun and others to proclaim the words, brave men Wei Chen and others to assist the decision, and Commandant of the Guard Lu Bode to lead troops and encamp at Guiyang awaiting the envoys.

sentences.zh: 南越王年少，太后中國人；

translations.literal: The King of Southern Yue was young; the Queen Dowager was a person of the central lands;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Southern Yue was young; the Queen Dowager was a person of the central lands;

sentences.zh: 安國少季往，復與私通，國人頗知之，多不附太后。

translations.literal: when Anguo Shaoji went, he again had a private liaison; the people of the state largely knew it and mostly did not attach themselves to the Queen Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: when Anguo Shaoji went, he again had a private liaison; the people of the state largely knew it and mostly did not attach themselves to the Queen Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后恐亂起，亦欲倚漢威，數勸王及群臣求內屬；

translations.literal: The Queen Dowager feared disorder would arise and also wished to rely on Han's authority; she repeatedly urged the king and the ministers to seek inner affiliation;
translations.idiomatic: The Queen Dowager feared disorder would arise and also wished to rely on Han's authority; she repeatedly urged the king and the ministers to seek inner affiliation;

sentences.zh: 即因使者上書，請比內諸侯，三歲一朝，除邊關。

translations.literal: thereupon through the envoys she memorialized, requesting to be comparable to inner feudal lords, attending court once every three years, and removing frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: thereupon through the envoys she memorialized, requesting to be comparable to inner feudal lords, attending court once every three years, and removing frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 於是天子許之，賜其丞相呂嘉銀印及內史、中尉、太傅印，餘得自置；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven granted it, bestowing on their Chancellor Lü Jia a silver seal and seals for Inner Scribe, Commandant of the Guards, and Grand Tutor; the rest they might appoint themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor granted it, bestowing on their Chancellor Lü Jia a silver seal and seals for Inner Scribe, Commandant of the Guards, and Grand Tutor; the rest they might appoint themselves;

sentences.zh: 除其故黥、劓刑，用漢法，比內諸侯。

translations.literal: abolishing their former tattooing and nose-cutting punishments, using Han law, comparable to inner feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: abolishing their former tattooing and nose-cutting punishments, using Han law, comparable to inner feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 使者皆留，填撫之。

translations.literal: The envoys all remained to fill and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys all remained to fill and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: ----8上行幸雍，且郊，或曰：「五帝，泰一之佐也。

translations.literal: ----8 The emperor traveled in favor to Yong and was about to perform suburban sacrifice; someone said: "The Five Emperors are assistants to the Grand Unity.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The emperor traveled in favor to Yong and was about to perform suburban sacrifice; someone said, "The Five Emperors are assistants to the Grand Unity.

sentences.zh: 宜立泰一，而上親郊。

translations.literal: The Grand Unity ought to be established, and the emperor should personally perform suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Unity ought to be established, and the emperor should personally perform suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」上疑未定。

translations.literal: " The emperor was doubtful and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was doubtful and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 齊人公孫卿曰：「今年得寶鼎，其冬辛巳朔旦冬至，與黃帝時等。

translations.literal: The man of Qi Gongsun Qing said: "This year the precious ding was obtained; this winter on xinsi, the new moon at dawn on the winter solstice, equals the time of the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The man of Qi Gongsun Qing said, "This year the precious ding was obtained; this winter on xinsi, the new moon at dawn on the winter solstice, equals the time of the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」卿有札書曰：「黃帝得寶鼎，是歲己酉朔旦冬至，凡三百八十年，黃帝仙登於天。

translations.literal: " Qing had a letter saying: "The Yellow Emperor obtained the precious tripod; that year, on jiyou new year's day at dawn on the winter solstice—in all three hundred eighty years—the Yellow Emperor ascended as an immortal to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing had a letter saying, "The Yellow Emperor obtained the precious tripod; that year, on jiyou new year's day at dawn on the winter solstice—in all three hundred eighty years—the Yellow Emperor ascended as an immortal to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」因嬖人奏之。

translations.literal: " He had a favorite present it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " He had a favorite present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，召問，卿對曰：「受此書申公，申公曰：『漢興復當黃帝之時，漢之聖者在高祖之孫且曾孫也。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and summoned him to question; Qing replied, saying: "I received this book from Lord Shen; Lord Shen said: 'When Han rises it will again reach the Yellow Emperor's time; Han's sage will be a grandson and great-grandson of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and summoned him for questioning; Qing replied, "I received this book from Lord Shen; Lord Shen said, 'When Han rises it will again reach the Yellow Emperor's time; Han's sage will be a grandson and great-grandson of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 寶鼎出而與神通，黃帝接萬靈明庭，明庭者甘泉也。

translations.literal: When the precious tripod appears one communicates with spirits; the Yellow Emperor received the myriad spirits at the Bright Court—the Bright Court is Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: When the precious tripod appears one communicates with the spirits; the Yellow Emperor received the myriad spirits at the Bright Court—and the Bright Court is Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: 黃帝采首山銅，鑄鼎於荊山下，鼎既成，有龍垂鬍髯下迎黃帝，黃帝上騎龍，與群臣後宮七十餘人俱登天。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor gathered copper from Mount Shou, cast the tripod below Mount Jing; when the tripod was complete a dragon lowered its beard and whiskers to welcome the Yellow Emperor; the Yellow Emperor mounted the dragon, and with over seventy ministers and palace women together ascended Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor gathered copper from Mount Shou and cast the tripod below Mount Jing; when the tripod was complete a dragon lowered its beard and whiskers to welcome the Yellow Emperor; the Yellow Emperor mounted the dragon, and with more than seventy ministers and palace women together ascended Heaven.

sentences.zh: 』」於是天子曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: '" Thereupon the Son of Heaven said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: '" Thereupon the Son of Heaven said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 誠得如黃帝，吾視去妻子如脫屣耳！

translations.literal: If I could truly be like the Yellow Emperor, I would regard leaving wife and children like casting off worn shoes!
translations.idiomatic: If I could truly be like the Yellow Emperor, I would regard leaving wife and children like casting off worn shoes!

sentences.zh: 」拜卿為郎，使東候神於太室。

translations.literal: " He appointed Qing as Gentleman and sent him east to await spirits at the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed Qing as Gentleman and sent him east to await spirits at the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上祠五畤於雍，遂逾隴，西登崆峒。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor sacrificed at the Five Altars in Yong, then crossed Long, and climbed west to Kongtong.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor sacrificed at the Five Altars in Yong, then crossed Long, and climbed west to Kongtong.

sentences.zh: 隴西守以行往卒，天子從官不得食，惶恐，自殺。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Longxi, because the journey pressed the conscripts, left the emperor's attendants without food; in fear and trembling he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Longxi, because the journey pressed the conscripts, left the emperor's attendants without food; in fear and trembling he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 於是上北出蕭關，從數萬騎獵新秦中，以勒邊兵而歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor went north out through Xiaoguan, followed by several tens of thousands of horsemen hunting in the new Qin interior, to review the border troops and return.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor went north out through Xiaoguan, followed by several tens of thousands of horsemen hunting in the new Qin interior, to review the border troops and return.

sentences.zh: 新秦中或千里無亭徼，於是誅北地太守以下。

translations.literal: In the new Qin interior there were places a thousand li without beacon towers or frontier posts; thereupon he executed the Administrator of Beidi and those below.
translations.idiomatic: In the new Qin interior there were places a thousand li without beacon towers or frontier posts; thereupon he executed the Administrator of Beidi and those below.

sentences.zh: 上又幸甘泉，立泰一祠壇，所用祠具如雍一畤而有加焉。

translations.literal: The emperor again visited Sweet Springs, established the Grand Unity sacrificial altar; the sacrificial implements used were like those at Yong's single altar but with additions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again visited Sweet Springs and established the Grand Unity sacrificial altar; the sacrificial implements used were like those at Yong's single altar but with additions.

sentences.zh: 五帝壇環居其下四方地，為醊食群神從者及北斗-{云}-。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors' altar ringed the ground below on four sides, making libation feasts for the attendant spirits of the host and the Northern Dipper -{yun}-.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors' altar ringed the ground below on four sides, making libation feasts for the attendant spirits of the host and the Northern Dipper -{yun}-.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛巳朔，冬至，昧爽，天子始郊拜泰一，朝朝日，夕夕月則揖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinsi new moon, the winter solstice, at gray dawn the Son of Heaven first suburban-sacrificed and bowed to Grand Unity; in the morning he faced the sun, in the evening he faced the moon and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinsi new moon, at the winter solstice, at gray dawn the Son of Heaven first suburban-sacrificed and bowed to Grand Unity; in the morning he faced the sun, in the evening he faced the moon and bowed.

sentences.zh: 其祠，列火滿壇，壇旁亨炊具。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice fires were ranged filling the altar; beside the altar cooking vessels were set to boil.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice fires were ranged filling the altar; beside the altar cooking vessels were set to boil.

sentences.zh: 有司云：「祠上有光。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: "Above the altar there was light.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported, "Above the altar there was light.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「晝有黃氣上屬天。

translations.literal: " They also reported: "By day yellow vapor rose up connecting to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " They also reported, "By day yellow vapor rose up connecting to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」太史令談、祠官寬舒等請三歲天子一郊見，詔從之。

translations.literal: " Grand Astrologer Tan, Sacrifice Officer Kuanshu and others requested that once every three years the Son of Heaven perform one suburban audience; an edict followed their request.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Astrologer Tan, Sacrifice Officer Kuanshu, and others requested that once every three years the Son of Heaven perform one suburban audience; an edict followed their request.

sentences.zh: ----2南越王、王太后飭治行裝，重賫為入朝具。

translations.literal: ----2 The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother ordered their travel gear prepared and sent heavy gifts as equipment for entering court.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The King of Nanyue and the Queen Mother ordered their travel gear prepared and sent heavy gifts as equipment for entering court.

sentences.zh: 其相呂嘉，年長矣，相三王，宗旅仕宦為長吏者七十餘人，男盡尚王女，女盡嫁王子弟、宗室，及蒼梧秦王有連，其居國中甚重，得眾心愈於王。

translations.literal: His Chancellor Lu Jia was advanced in years, had served three kings; over seventy clansmen in office as senior officials—all the men had married the king's daughters, all the women had married the king's sons, younger brothers, and imperial clansmen—and he was connected with the King of Cangwu; his standing in the state was very weighty, and he won the people's hearts more than the king.
translations.idiomatic: His Chancellor Lu Jia was advanced in years and had served three kings; more than seventy clansmen held office as senior officials—all the men had married the king's daughters, all the women had married the king's sons, younger brothers, and imperial clansmen—and he was connected with the King of Cangwu; his standing in the state was very weighty, and he won the people's hearts more than the king.

sentences.zh: 王之上書，數諫止王，王弗聽；
